blocks.html:
This page describes the legacy Docker Compose stack (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration): the core services that make up Deploy App, the miniwerk provisioner that bootstraps a deployment, and how product integrations attach to the composition. It is for developers and operators who need to navigate the compose file rather than deploy it — for deployment steps see Deploy with Docker Compose. The Kubernetes counterpart of this page is Core services.

Core services

Everything lives in a single docker-compose.yml. The core of Deploy App — codename RASENMAEHER — is this set of compose services (image tags shown with the default RELEASE_TAG of 2.9.0):

Compose service Image (defaults) Role
rmapi ghcr.io/pvarki/rmapi:1.16.0-260523-d2.9.0 RASENMAEHER core API (FastAPI, port 8000) — enrollment, invites, cert issuance orchestration
rmui ghcr.io/pvarki/rmui:2.3.1-260506-default-d2.9.0 One-shot: copies the built React UI into the rmui_files volume
rmnginx ghcr.io/pvarki/nginx:1.31-d2.9.0 Main edge proxy on :443 — serves the UI, proxies /api/ to rmapi:8000
nginx_templates ghcr.io/pvarki/nginx:templates-d2.9.0 One-shot: delivers nginx config templates into the nginx_templates volume
keycloak ghcr.io/pvarki/keycloak:24.0.5-d2.9.0 OIDC identity provider, terminates its own TLS on :9443 (published directly, KC_HOSTNAME = kc.<domain>)
keycloak-init adorsys/keycloak-config-cli:6.1.6-24 One-shot: imports the RASENMAEHER realm into Keycloak over internal HTTP :8080
openldap ghcr.io/pvarki/openldap:1.0.0-d2.9.0 User directory (root dc=example,dc=org), LDAP :1389 internal, LDAPS :1636 published
postgres postgis/postgis:15-3.4 Single shared PostgreSQL for everything (PostGIS because TAK needs it)
autoheal willfarrell/autoheal:latest Watches the Docker socket and restarts containers labeled autoheal=true that go unhealthy

blocks.html:
Key details:

  • rmnginx serves three hostnames (<domain>, mtls.<domain>, synapse.<domain>) from one container — server blocks are detailed on Networking & subdomains (legacy).
  • rmui is not a running server: it exits after copying the built UI into rmui_files, and rmnginx gates on service_completed_successfully. Product UI bundles are delivered the same way through the ui_files volume, served under /ui/.
  • Keycloak is not behind rmnginx — it publishes 9443 itself with --https-client-auth=request and gets its TLS certificate from the shared le_certs volume. It federates users from openldap, and keycloak-init (re)applies the realm config from keycloak/keycloak-config/ with LDAP_CONNECTION_URL: ldap://openldap:1389.
  • postgres is one shared instance on the dbnet network; init scripts in pg_init/ create separate roles and databases: keycloak, raesenmaeher, tak, battlelog, rmmtx, synapse.
  • rmapi persists its JWT signing key in the rmapi_data volume (JWT_PRIVKEY_PATH=/data/persistent/private/rm_jwtsign.key) and reads its product registry from /pvarki (see miniwerk below). Several healthchecks in the stack are honest stubs (test: 'true' # FIXME), which is one reason autoheal exists.
  • Compose networks partition traffic: apinet, kcnet, canet, ocspnet, dbnet, intranet, productnet, taknet — each service joins only the networks it needs.

The CA side (cfssl, ocsp, ocsprest services) is covered on PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy).

miniwerk — the legacy provisioner

miniwerk (ghcr.io/pvarki/miniwerk:1.8.2-260524-d2.9.0, submodule python-rasenmaeher-miniwerk) is a one-shot job that runs before everything else — nearly every service in the composition has a depends_on: miniwerk: condition: service_completed_successfully gate. Its README calls it a "minimal KRAFTWERK emulation": it stands in for a central provisioning service so a full RASENMAEHER-plus-products deployment can run on any single VM. It does three things:

  1. Resolves the deployment's FQDN plan from **MW_PRODUCTS** — a <product>.<domain> plus mtls.<product>.<domain> pair per product; the subdomain model is on Networking & subdomains (legacy).
  2. Fetches one Let's Encrypt certificate covering all of those names into the shared le_certs volume; the certificate job is on PKI: CFSSL & miniwerk (legacy).
  3. Writes the KRAFTWERK manifests that introduce core and products to each other. Into /pvarkishares/rasenmaeher (mounted by rmapi at /pvarki) it writes kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init.json, mapping every product to its API URL (https://<product>.<domain>:4626/, plus a base path where configured — Battlelog's is /rmapi/ via MW_BL__API_BASE), user URL and expected certificate CN (certcn: <product>.<domain>). Into each /pvarkishares/<product> (mounted by that product's integration API at /pvarki) it writes a kraftwerk-init.json with the RASENMAEHER base URIs and a one-time CSR JWT valid for 24 hours. miniwerk's own JWT public key (kraftwerk.pub) is copied into every share, so rmapi can verify the tokens miniwerk issued. Existing manifests are never overwritten — a deployment keeps its identity across restarts.

Per-product ports are also miniwerk settings (MW_TAK__API_PORT, MW_MTX__USER_PORT, …), all defaulting the API side to 4626 — which is where the product proxy comes in.

Product integration APIs

Each product ships an integration API container — the product side of the RASENMAEHER API contract. In the legacy stack these are:

Product Compose service Image (defaults) Container port Public route
TAK takrmapi ghcr.io/pvarki/takrmapi:1.13.0-260508-tak5.7-RELEASE-32-d2.9.0 8003 tak.<domain>:4626
MediaMTX rmmtx ghcr.io/pvarki/rmmtx:1.6.0-260513-d2.9.0 8005 mtx.<domain>:4626
Matrix matrixrmapi ghcr.io/pvarki/matrixrmapi:1.1.1-260512-d2.9.0 8012 matrix.<domain>:4626
Battlelog blapi ghcr.io/pvarki/blapi:1.1.0-d2.9.0 3000 bl.<domain>:4626

(A fifth, the fake reference product rmfpapi from submodule fpintegration, runs only in the local/dev compositions — but its NGINX_FP_UPSTREAM variables must still be defined on productsnginx for the template to render.)

All four are fronted by productsnginx on port **4626**, client certificate required — routing and the cert-free 4627 ephemeral listener are detailed on Networking & subdomains (legacy).

Attaching a product therefore touches several places at once: an entry in MW_PRODUCTS (plus a ProductSettings block in miniwerk's config), DNS records for <product>.<domain> and mtls.<product>.<domain>, NGINX_<PRODUCT>_UPSTREAM variables on productsnginx plus a line in the nginx template's host map, and the product's own compose service. There is no single registry — the compose file, miniwerk and the nginx templates must agree.

End to end, a product attaches like this:

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant MW as miniwerk
    participant LE as LetsEncrypt
    participant PROD as productAPI
    participant RM as rmapi
    participant NG as productsnginx
    participant EUD as client

    Note over MW: MW_PRODUCTS lists tak, kc, bl, mtx, matrix, synapse
    MW->>LE: certbot HTTP-01 for product.domain and mtls.product.domain
    LE-->>MW: certificate written to le_certs volume
    MW->>PROD: kraftwerk-init.json via /pvarki volume (URLs + 24h CSR JWT)
    MW->>RM: product entry in kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init.json (API URL + certcn)
    PROD->>RM: kw_product_init POSTs CSR to /api/v1/product/sign_csr with the JWT
    RM-->>PROD: signed mTLS client cert, CN = product.domain
    EUD->>NG: https to product.domain port 4626 with client cert
    NG->>NG: verify cert against ca_chain.pem plus OCSP
    NG->>PROD: proxy to container port with X-ClientCert-DN header

blocks.html:
The kw_product_init step is a small Go helper (golang-kraftwerk-init-helper-cli, built by the kwinit compose service) baked into product images: on first boot it reads /pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json, generates a keypair and CSR for <product>.<domain>, and exchanges the one-time JWT for a signed mTLS client certificate at rmapi's /api/v1/product/sign_csr. From then on, rmapi and the product authenticate each other with mutual TLS: rmapi pins the product's expected certcn, and the product calls back through mtls.<domain>.

Kubernetes contrast. On the Kubernetes platform this whole machinery is gone: there is no miniwerk, no shared nginx to edit and no port 4626. A product attaches by shipping Kubernetes manifests — its own namespace, Deployment, IngressRoute and a kraftwerk-init.json ConfigMap — and registering itself in rmapi's product registry ConfigMap. See Integration pattern and Register your integration (Kubernetes).

The submodule model

The integration repo contains almost no application code. Every component lives in its own repository and is pulled in as a git submodule — .gitmodules pins 14 of them, including api (python-rasenmaeher-api), uiv2 (react-rasenmaeher-ui-v2), miniwerk, cfssl, keycloak, takserver, takintegration, mtxauthz, matrixrmapi, battlelog, synapse, fpintegration, kw_product_init and kc_client_init. The compose file's build: contexts point straight into these directories, so a checkout of the integration repo at a given tag is a complete, reproducible build recipe:

git clone --recurse-submodules -j8 git@github.com:pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration.git
## later, after checking out a tag or pulling:
git submodule update --init --recursive

The consequence for development: a change never lands in the composition directly. You commit and push in the component's own repository (each submodule directory is a full working repo), and then a PR against docker-rasenmaeher-integration bumps the submodule pointer to the new commit — that pointer bump is what actually changes which code a deployment runs. Release tags on the integration repo capture a known-good combination of all submodule SHAs, which is why the README recommends deploying from tags. The day-to-day edit-rebuild loop inside this structure is described in Iterate on the core API (Docker Compose).
